newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end sharply up on firm cash tone.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end sharply up on firm cash tone.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended sharply higher Monday, boosted by heavy commercial buying and a firm tone in Southern Plains cash cattle markets, CME traders said.
Feeder cattle futures ended with moderate gains.
R.B.& H. Financial Services and R.J. O'Brien were noted buyers in early live cattle futures trade, while midsession activity was very light, pit sources said.
Futures were lifted by scattered talk that a small number of fed cattle traded at $71.00 per cwt in Texas, floor sources said. That is $1.00 higher than last week's top of $70.00.
"If the packer is buying any cattle on Monday, that says that he's desparate and needs cattle," one floor trader said.
Most fed cattle markets were very quiet. Packer bids ranged from $69.00 to $70.00, while feedlots asked $71.00 to $72.00, cash connected sources said.
Good retail sales of beef over the weekend also helped generate the bullish tone in cattle, floor traders said.
"The beef is what drove us higher this morning (Monday)," one trader with ties to the cash market said. "Weekend clearance (sales) were phenomenal."
At midday, wholesale beef prices were mostly higher in light sales volume, USDA reported.
Feeder cattle futures ended higher on strength borrowed from live cattle, but a decline in the latest CME feeder index of $0.07 to $62.85 limited gains, traders said.

Live cattle ended up 0.050 to up 0.875 cent a lb, with December up 0.875 cent at $66.675 and February up 0.750 at $63.525. Feeder cattle futures ended up 0.075 to up 0.525, with November up 0.075 at $62.325 cent per lb.
